_how: Eye-judged against the 2004 captures at matched angles (designer front + the old client's close camera, heads row of each <opt>_vs_2004 sheet). Face checklist: bold dark eye slits with the small outer drop, no brow blocks, no mouth (beard covers it on the man), egg head with a slightly pointed crown, small close ears, face planes readable in the shading, the default man's broad goatee. Shading checklist: the 2004 renderer shows big flat panels on the clothes and the face planes, only gentle curves (legs, arms) look smooth; colours read darker and contrastier in game.

face.note: all the 2004 features (bold slits + drop, no brows / mouth, egg head, small ears, broad goatee, faceted face planes); ours reads a touch softer and less contrasty than the reference face at the game camera

shading.note: panel shading (smooth under 36 deg) = the reference's flat clothing panels and face planes; our 6-sided limbs facet a little harder than the reference's trouser gradients

face.note: same features plus a faint mouth line; the smoother shading softens the face planes the reference shows

shading.note: smooth under 65 deg: limbs match the reference's gradients, but the clothes lose the big flat panels and read rounder / more modern than 2004

face.note: stylised: small brows, eye boxes, a mouth line and a slightly larger head -- friendlier, clearly less 2004

shading.note: hard facets everywhere (smooth only under 12 deg): a papercraft low-poly look, flatter and harder than the 2004 renderer
